\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دماغ} (dimāgh)}{دماغ (dimāgh)}]{\ur{دماغ} (dimāgh) — the brain; the mind}

\label{lesson:UR-C464-dimagh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to whisper, then the Urdu for speechless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دماغ}}
\textbf{\ur{دماغ}} — \emph{dimāgh} — \textquotedblleft{}the brain; the mind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دماغ} \ur{جسم} \ur{کو} \ur{چلاتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dimāgh jism ko chalātā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The brain runs the body.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دماغ}} (\emph{dimāgh}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{dimāgh}, \textquotedblleft{}brain\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dimāgh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dimāgh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dimāgh jism ko chalātā hai.} — The brain runs the body.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to whisper, then the Urdu for speechless, then say \emph{dimāgh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{دماغ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The brain; the mind\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معدہ} (medā)}{معدہ (medā)}]{\ur{معدہ} (medā) — the stomach as an organ}

\label{lesson:UR-C464-meda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the brain, then the Urdu for a kidney.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معدہ}}
\textbf{\ur{معدہ}} — \emph{medā} — \textquotedblleft{}the stomach as an organ\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{معدہ} \ur{کمزور} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā medā kamzor hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have a weak stomach.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معدہ}} (\emph{medā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{maʿida}, \textquotedblleft{}stomach\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ur{پیٹ}} is the belly you can point to.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for the brain, then the Urdu for a kidney, then say \emph{medā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{آنت} (āṅt)}{آنت (āṅt)}]{\ur{آنت} (āṅt) — an intestine}

\label{lesson:UR-C464-ant}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a kidney, then the Urdu for the stomach as an organ.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{آنت}}
\textbf{\ur{آنت}} — \emph{āṅt} — \textquotedblleft{}an intestine\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پیٹ} \ur{میں} \ur{لمبی} \ur{آنتیں} \ur{ہوتی} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رگ} (rag)}{رگ (rag)}]{\ur{رگ} (rag) — a vein}

\label{lesson:UR-C464-rag}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the stomach as an organ, then the Urdu for an intestine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رگ}}
\textbf{\ur{رگ}} — \emph{rag} — \textquotedblleft{}a vein\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نرس} \ur{نے} \ur{رگ} \ur{سے} \ur{خون} \ur{لیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nars ne rag se khūn liyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رگ}} (\emph{rag}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{rag}, \textquotedblleft{}vein, sinew\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
